*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID -19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor ’s Executive Order N- 29- 20 (https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp -
content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20 -N -29 -20 -EO.pdf ).

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting of September 15,
2020, at 1:00 P.M. for closed session as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for consideration
  by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers
  Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at yhorton@cityofinglewood.org , and Deputy
  City Clerk aphillips@cityofinglewood.org . To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to
  consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the
  email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and
  agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to the close of the public hearings, will be made part of
  the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2.  By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public can participate in
  the meeting by telephone to listen and make comments by using the following:

  l Dial-In: 1-669 -900-6833 (Meeting ID: 996 1738 7790).
  l All interested parties who wished to provide public comments telephonically may join the conference at 12:50 p.m.
  l If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception. Calls from landline phones are
  highly recommended.

** The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to address the Legislative Body on Closed Session Items.

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting of September 15,
2020, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2.  By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public can participate in
  the meeting by telephone to listen and make comments noting the following:

  l The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join the conference 5 minutes prior.
  l If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception. Calls from landline phones are
  highly recommended.
  l If you are watching the meeting via Facebook Live or Channel 35 while also accessing the phone line, it is requested

  making public comments on the phone line, you will be inaudible due to feedback.
  l Dial -In: 1 -888-251 -2949 or 1-215 -861-0694 using the specific access codes detailed below for the respective City Council
  Dates:

  3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider for details.
  l Live on -line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/.
   ¡ September 22, 2020 – Access Code: 64848997# (wait 5 seconds and press # again)
  ¡ September 29, 2020 – Access Code: 2424497# (wait 5 seconds and press # again)

  3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider for details.
  l Live on -line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/.

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting; however,
members of the public who wish to orally address the Legislative Body must use the public access option 2.

ACCESSIBILITY : If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with
Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in
implementation thereof. Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or
translation services in order to observe and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable
modification, accommodation, or service by contacting the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-
412-5280, FAX at 310 -412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood,
CA 90301 or via email to yhorton@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled
meeting.

Inglewood, California
  September 15, 2020

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
Tuesday, September 15, 2020, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

MAYOR PRO TEM APPOINTMENT. It was moved by Council Member
Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Dotson that the City Council does
hereby appoint Council Member Morales as Mayor Pro Tem for Closed Session.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Council Members Dotson, Padilla, and Morales;
Noes:  None; and
Absent:  Mayor Butts, and Council Member Franklin.

Mayor Pro Tem Morales called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour
of 1:01 p.m.
The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Council Members Dotson, Padilla, and Mayor Pro
  Tem Morales; and
  Absent:  Mayor Butts, and Council Member Franklin.
City officials and personnel present for Closed Session were as follows:

  Aisha Thompson  Acting City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor
Pro Tem Morales inquired if there were any persons present who wished to
address the City Council on Closed Session Item Nos. CS-1 and CS-2.

Caller (Name Unknown) spoke concerning Agenda Item No. CS-1, Closed
Session- Labor Negotiations with Service Employees International Union (SEIU);
Inglewood Police Officers Associations (IPOA); Inglewood Police Management
Association (IPMA).

Mayor Pro Tem Morales recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:05 p.m. for
Closed Session Item Nos. CS-1 and CS-2.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing
Authority, at the hour of 2:05 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary
announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority  Chairman  Butts,  Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and
  Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.

City/Successor Agency / Housing Authority officials and personnel present were
as follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*

  1
 September 15, 2020

  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons
  present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
  Authority on any item on the Agenda.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke concerning Agenda Item Nos. DR-1, resolution to
  approve changes to the HOME Policies and Procedures Manual, and O-1, the
  revised and updated Investment Policy and Procedures.

  Caller (Name Unknown), spoke concerning Agenda Item No. O-1, the revised and
  updated Investment Policy and Procedures.

  Diane Sambrano spoke concerning Agenda Item No. O-1, the revised and updated
  Investment Policy and Procedures.

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded
  by Council Member /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member
  Dotson that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated September 11, 2020, in the amount of
  $3,687,190.21, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor/Successor
  Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 125  CLAIMS REJECTED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney
  recommending the following:
  A. Reject Claims filed pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1. Ladislao Hernandez for alleged property damage; repair equipment on March
  20, 2020.
  2. Mark Lucaj for alleged vehicle damage; CDS Republic forklift on June 29,
  2020.
  3. Gricela Madrigal for alleged vehicle damage; road condition on June 10,
  2020.
  B. Return Late Claim Pursuant to Government Code Section 912:
  1. Jacquelyn Huizar for alleged property seizure; asset forfeiture warrant.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member
  Dotson, that the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject the claims listed as A-1
  through A-3; and 2) Return Late Claim listed as B-1. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 301  AGREEMENT NO. 20-257 APPROVED – STEVEN R. NORRIS &
  ASSOCIATES, INC. Staff report dated September 15, 2020, was presented
  recommending approval of an agreement with Steven R. Norris & Associates Inc.,
  dba Norris Realty Advisors to conduct real estate appraisal services for the IBEC
  Project.

  2
 September 15, 2020

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 20-257 in the
  amount of $67,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  PAYMENT OF INVOICES AUTHORIZED – L & M FOOTWEAR, INC.,
  DBA SHOETERIA. Staff report dated September 15, 2020, was presented
  recommending authorization to pay invoices submitted by L & M Footwear, Inc.,
  dba Shoeteria for the provision of safety boots/shoes to employees working in the
  areas of hazardous conditions.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of
  $1,631.21. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 183  PAYMENT OF INVOICES AUTHORIZED – ROBERTO TRIGUEROS
  DBA OCEAN N SUN HEATING & AIR CONDITIONING. Staff report
  dated September 15, 2020, was presented recommending authorization to pay
  Invoice No. 10256 submitted by Roberto Trigueros dba Ocean N Sun Heating &
  Air Conditioning for emergency repairs to the City Hall Domestic Water Pumps
  Isolated Valves.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Franklin that the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of
  $12,850. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 183  PAYMENT OF INVOICES AUTHORIZED – JOHNSON CONTROLS
  FIRE PROTECTION, LP. Staff report dated September 15, 2020, was
  presented recommending authorization to pay invoices submitted by Johnson
  Controls Fire Protection, LP, for the purchase and installation of a new fire alarm
  panel system at the Inglewood Civic Center.
  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of
  $100,070.01. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 20-258 APPROVED –
  KPPF, INC. Staff report dated September 15, 2020, was presented
  recommending award of contract and approval of an agreement with KPPF, Inc.,
  for the seismic retrofit design of the Civic Center buildings and preparation of the
  plans, specifications, and construction cost estimate.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement
  No. 20-258 in the amount of $1,510,608 (includes a ten percent (10%)
  contingency in the amount of $137,328). The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  3
 September 15, 2020

  183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 20-259 APPROVED –
  DEGENKOLB ENGINEERS. Staff report dated September 15, 2020, was
  presented recommending award of contract and approval of an agreement with
  Degenkolb Engineers to conduct an independent review and oversight of the
  Civic Center seismic retrofit design process.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement
  No. 20-259 in the amount of $201,624.50 (includes a ten percent (10%)
  contingency in the amount of $18,329.50). The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  131.8  RESOLUTION NO. 20-130 ADOPTED – APPROVAL OF CHANGES TO
  THE HOME POLICIES AND PROCEDURES MANUAL. Staff report dated
  September 15, 2020, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution to
  approve changes to the HOME Policies and Procedures Manual for the
  administration of the HOME program and adopt an update manual to supersede
  any prior version.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that Resolution No. 20-130 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING CHANGES TO THE
  HOME PROGRAM POLICIES AND PROCEDURES MANUAL AND
  ADOPTING AN UPDATED MANUAL INCORPORATING SAID
  CHANGES

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  101  REVISED AND UPDATED INVESTMENT POLICY AND PROCEDURES
  ADOPTED; ORDINANCE NO. 20-16 INTRODUCED – REASSIGNMENT
  OF CITY DUTIES. Staff report dated September 15, 2020, was presented
  recommending adoption of the revised and updated Investment Policy and
  Procedures delegating the authority to the Finance Director, or designee, to invest
  all of the City’s Funds except for an amount of no more than $50,000 to be
  managed by the City Treasurer, and the introduction of an Ordinance amending
  the Inglewood Municipal Code for the reassignment of City duties.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby adopt the revised and updated
  Investment Policy and Procedures. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  Whereupon, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Franklin that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  4
 September 15, 2020

  Furthermore, Ordinance No. 20-16 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA AMENDING CHAPTER 2, ARTICLE 7
  (CITY FUNDS – BUDGETARY PROCEDURES) AND ARTICLE 9
  (CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT); AMENDING CHAPTER 8,
  ARTICLE 3 (PERMITS); AND AMENDING CHAPTER 10, ARTICLE
  5 (CURBS, SIDEWALKS AND PARKWAYS)

  was introduced by Council Member Franklin.

 132.6  CLOSED SESSION – CONFIDENTIAL – LABOR NEGOTIATIONS
  WITH SEIU, IPOA AND IPMA.  Closed session – Confidential –
  Attorney/Client Privileged; Conference with Labor Negotiator Pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54957.6; Name of the Agency Negotiator: Jose O.
  Cortes, Human Resources Director; Name of Organizations Representing
  Employees; Service Employees International Union (SEIU); Inglewood Police
  Officers Associations (IPOA); Inglewood Police Management Association
  (IPMA).

  Status was given; Direction given to staff.

 132.6  CLOSED SESSION – CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEY/CLIENT
  PRIVILEDGED; PENDING LITIGATION; YOLANDA TOBIN V. CITY
  OF INGLEWOOD, ET AL.; LASC CASE NO. 19STCV08190. Closed session
  – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged; Pending Litigation Pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1); Yolanda Tobin v. City of Inglewood, et
  al.; LASC Case No. 19STCV08190.

  Status given, Direction given to staff.
  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Rick Ford stated he would like the City Council to cancel rent.  He also
  commented that he would like to see Community Room A re-opened.

  Caller (Name Unknown), spoke concerning the rent in the City of Inglewood.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke concerning the Clippers Arena.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the
  meeting adjourned at the hour of 2:46 p.m.

  Approved this 27th day of April, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
